title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TOMMY'S WINTER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Tommy Nguyen, a furnace repairman who moved from Houston to Anchorage, Alaska, for a job.
He knew nobody. And by four in the afternoon, it was dark.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE 2 A.M. CALL
segments.quote: Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for a kindness.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Tommy fixed furnaces all day, then ate dinner alone.
One night at two in the morning, Pete Larsen, a retired fisherman, called with no heat.
Tommy fixed it fast and grabbed his keys. Then he saw the note his boss had taped in the van, from Seneca, the Roman thinker:
Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for a kindness.
So Tommy stayed for coffee. Pete invited him to curling night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE ICE
segments.quote: In three words I can sum up everything I've learned about life: it goes on.
segments.author: Robert Frost
lines: A guy from Houston, on ice. Tommy fell flat on his back three times.
Pete helped him up, laughing, and quoted the poet Robert Frost:
In three words I can sum up everything I've learned about life: it goes on.
So Tommy came back the next Thursday. And the next. He fell less every week.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE HEATER
segments.quote: The language of friendship is not words but meanings.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: But Tommy was shy. At the club, he hardly said a word.
Then the club's old heater broke. Tommy remembered his mom's fridge magnet, from Henry David Thoreau:
The language of friendship is not words but meanings.
So he fixed the heater for free. The next week, Bev, the team captain, saved him a seat.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: NO HEAT
segments.quote: What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?
segments.author: George Eliot
lines: In January, Tommy's own furnace died. The furnace guy, with no furnace.
It was twenty below, and he was too proud to ask for help.
Bev, a librarian, texted him a line from George Eliot, the English novelist:
What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?
Tommy said yes. He spent the week on Pete's couch. Pete snores like a snowplow.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE OFFER
segments.quote: A friend is, as it were, a second self.
segments.author: Cicero
lines: In March, his old boss in Houston called. Come home. Warm weather. Better pay.
Tommy started packing. Pete sat on a box and quoted Cicero:
A friend is, as it were, a second self.
So if you leave, Pete said, half of me moves to Texas. Tommy unpacked the box.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: CHILI NIGHT
segments.quote: A man, Sir, should keep his friendship in constant repair.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: Now Tommy has his own note in the van, from Samuel Johnson, the English writer:
A man, Sir, should keep his friendship in constant repair.
So once a month, he cooks Texas chili for the club. And on Sundays, he calls his old friends in Houston.
He fixes furnaces all day. On Thursdays, he fixes the other thing.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be kind. Keep going. Show it. Accept help. Value friends. Keep them in repair.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Stay for the coffee. Get back up. Show it, don't say it. Let people help. Treasure your friends. And keep them in good repair.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And go easy on the chili.
